items.text: Every year, millions of Christmas trees end up in landfills, but an Illinois farm has a greener solution: feeding them to Nigerian pygmy goats! Urban Growers Collective, a nonprofit in Chicago, is accepting undecorated pine trees at South Chicago Farm until January 11. These trees are a nutritious snack for their 15 goats, providing vitamins A and C while promoting digestive health and reducing parasites. Goats love eating the bark, branches, and needles, which act as natural composters . However, donated trees must be free of decorations, tinsel , hooks, or fire-retardant sprays , as these can harm the animals. For those unable to donate trees to the farm, Chicago’s citywide recycling program runs from January 11–25, offering 27 drop-off sites. Recycled trees will be turned into mulch for parks, forests, and residents. Even broken holiday lights can be recycled at over 30 locations across Chicago through January 31, ensuring a more sustainable holiday season. Difficult words: composter (natural material that decomposes into soil), tinsel (long, shiny, colored string used as a decoration at Christmas), fire-retardant spray (a chemical spray that reduces fire risk), mulch (ground-up wood or leaves used in gardening). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Instead of throwing your Christmas tree in the trash, why not give it to goats? Urban Growers Collective, a nonprofit in Chicago, is collecting old pine trees to feed their 15 Nigerian pygmy goats. The trees provide vitamins A and C and help keep the goats healthy. Residents can drop off undecorated trees at South Chicago Farm until January 11. Goats enjoy eating the bark, branches, and needles. But make sure the trees are free of decorations, hooks, and fire-retardant sprays , which can harm the animals. If donating to goats is not possible, Chicago’s recycling program runs from January 11–25. They will turn trees into mulch for parks and gardens. Broken holiday lights can also be recycled at special locations through January 31. Difficult words: nonprofit (an organization which makes money to help people, not for business), undecorated (without decorations or ornaments), fire-retardant spray (a spray which reduces fire), mulch (pieces of wood which we use in gardening). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Don’t throw away your Christmas tree! You can give it to goats instead. A Chicago farm is taking old pine trees to feed their 15 Nigerian pygmy goats. The trees are healthy for the goats. They give them vitamins A and C. You can drop off trees at South Chicago Farm until January 11. Make sure the trees do not have decorations, hooks , or fire sprays. These can hurt the goats. If you can’t give your tree to the goats, you can recycle it with the city. From January 11–25, you can bring your tree to one of 27 locations. The trees will turn into mulch for parks and gardens. Difficult words: hook (a curved device for catching or holding things), recycle (to use again), mulch (pieces of wood which we use in gardening). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poncho, an eight-year-old cocker spaniel, went viral thanks to his life-saving CPR skills. At a display of police dog skills in Madrid, the dog ran to his partner when he collapsed lifeless on the floor. The dog quickly began CPR, leaping and thudding onto the officer’s chest and even nestling his head onto the fallen policeman’s neck, as if he was checking for a pulse. Poncho repeated the procedure until his friend revived , and the crowd roared with applause. Difficult words: CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation – making the heart and breathing work again), leap (jump up high), thud (move, fall down), nestle (put something closely), revive (bring to life again), roar (be loud). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Poncho is an eight-year-old cocker spaniel from Madrid, and he is a very good police dog who could even save his partner’s life! At a show for police dogs, he ran to his partner who fell to the ground. He started jumping and thudding onto his chest to perform CPR . He even put his head onto the officer’s neck to check for a pulse . After doing this for a while, the police officer got up. The crowd loved the performance. Difficult words: thud (move with strong movements), CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation – making the heart and lungs work again), pulse (a heartbeat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Poncho is a police dog. He is from Madrid. He is eight years old. He is a very good dog. He performs at a show for police dogs. People especially love that he can perform CPR . His partner falls to the ground. He runs to him and tries to help him. He starts jumping on his chest . After doing this for a while, the officer gets up. Difficult words: perform (do, carry out), CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation – making the heart and lungs work again), chest (the front part of the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe has set a record by flying closer to the Sun than any other spacecraft. On Christmas Eve, it reached just 6.1 million km from the Sun’s surface, enduring temperatures of 1,400°C and harmful radiation that could have damaged its systems. Traveling at 692,000 kph, it became the fastest human-made object, equivalent to flying from London to New York in under 30 seconds. The probe survived thanks to a heat shield that kept its instruments cool. Scientists believe the data it collects will help answer why the Sun’s outer atmosphere, the corona , is much hotter than its surface. The corona, reaching millions of degrees, is key to understanding solar flares, magnetic fields , and space weather that affect Earth. Initial data will be analyzed starting in January, providing insights into the Sun’s behavior and its impact on our planet. Difficult words: radiation (energy from the Sun that can harm electronics), corona (the outermost layer of the Sun’s atmosphere), magnetic field (an invisible force around magnetic objects). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe flew closer to the Sun than ever before on Christmas Eve. It came within 6.1 million km of the Sun’s surface. The probe faced extreme heat of 1,400°C and dangerous radiation . It also became the fastest object ever made, traveling at 692,000 kph, faster than flying between London and New York in 30 seconds! The spacecraft has a special heat shield to protect its systems and keep them cool. It is studying the Sun’s corona, the outer layer of its atmosphere, which is hotter than the Sun’s surface. Scientists hope the probe’s data will explain how the Sun works. This information will help us understand space weather which can affect Earth. Difficult words: probe (spacecraft), radiation (dangerous energy from the Sun), shield (a piece of metal or other material which protects someone or something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

NASA’s Parker Solar Probe flies closer to the Sun than any other spacecraft. On Christmas Eve, it comes very close, 6.1 million km from the Sun. There is very high heat, 1,400°C, and dangerous energy from the Sun. The probe also becomes the fastest object people make. It moves at 692,000 kph. The spacecraft has a special cover which protects it from the Sun’s heat. It is studying the corona, the outside part of the Sun. This area is hotter than the Sun’s surface . Scientists want to know why. The probe will help us learn more about the Sun and how it affects Earth. Difficult words: probe (spacecraft), protect (to keep safe), surface (the outside or top layer of something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year brought many exciting advancements. Technological innovations included a titanium heart that kept a man alive until a transplant, and AI tools that improved cancer detection by identifying early warning signs. In medicine, groundbreaking trials included the first lung cancer vaccine, designed to help the immune system fight cancer cells. Besides this, Manuka honey was found to reduce breast cancer cell growth by 84%. A breakthrough in cervical cancer treatment reduced mortality by 40% with a new chemo-radiation method. In environmental progress, deforestation in the Amazon decreased by 31%, while efforts to restore the Great Barrier Reef included planting heat-resistant coral. Solar power grew rapidly, and China built the world’s largest solar farm. Social advancements included Thailand passing a same-sex marriage bill and the US capping insulin prices. Finally, space exploration achieved milestones like the first civilian spacewalk and NASA’s Solar Sail System for sunlight-powered spacecraft. Difficult words: groundbreaking (innovative and new), mortality (death rate), cap (to place a limit or restriction on prices). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This year was full of great news. In medicine, a lung cancer vaccine started trials to help the immune system fight cancer. A new treatment for cervical cancer reduced deaths by 40%. AI helped detect cancer early and save more lives. A titanium heart also helped a man live until he could get a real heart. The environment improved with less deforestation in the Amazon and new ways to save coral reefs. Solar power grew fast, with China building the biggest solar farm ever. Space had exciting news too, with the first civilian spacewalk and a new solar-powered spaceship idea from NASA. Social changes included Thailand’s new law for same-sex marriage and cheaper insulin for people in the US. Difficult words: cervical (relating to the cervix, the narrow lower part of the uterus), deforestation (clearing a wide area of trees), civilian (an ordinary person, not a soldier), insulin (a hormone which manages your blood sugar level). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This year is very exciting! In medicine, experts are testing a vaccine to help fight lung cancer. And a new treatment for cervical cancer helps save more lives. A special metal heart keeps a man alive until he gets a real one. AI also helps doctors find cancer early. The natural world sees good changes, too. The Amazon rainforest has less cutting of trees. People are helping coral reefs grow stronger. China builds the largest solar farm. Social changes included new same-sex marriage rules in Thailand and cheaper medicine for diabetes in the US. In space, there is the first walk by people who are not astronauts. Also, NASA makes a ship which uses energy from the sun to move. Difficult words: treatment (medical care), cervical (relating to the narrow lower part of a woman’s uterus), social (relating to people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A bear near Lake Tahoe in California trapped itself inside a car. Someone filmed the moment that a county sheriff’s deputy broke the window and allowed the bear to flee . Difficult words: trap (get stuck inside, not able to get out), county (an area in an American state), sheriff’s deputy (police officer), flee (run away). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In California, a bear got stuck inside a car, and a sheriff’s deputy broke the window to free the bear. It got out and ran away. Someone filmed the moment on video. Difficult words: stuck (not able to get out), sheriff’s deputy (a police officer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from California. A bear gets inside a car. It cannot get out. It is stuck . A sheriff’s deputy wants to help the bear. He breaks the window. The bear gets out of the car. It is free. Someone filmed all of this on video. Difficult words: be stuck (when you cannot get out of something), sheriff’s deputy (a police officer), filmed (past tense of ‘film’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The future of technology is rapidly changing, bringing innovations that are transforming industries and daily life. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are revolutionizing fields like healthcare, finance, and education by automating tasks and making intelligent decisions. 5G technology will provide faster internet speeds and connect more devices, enabling advancements in autonomous vehicles and smart cities. The Internet of Things (IoT) is creating networks of connected devices, improving efficiency in healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation. Blockchain, best known for cryptocurrencies, is enhancing security in industries such as finance and supply chains. Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) are making an impact on entertainment, education, and real estate by offering immersive experiences. Other important trends include Quantum Computing, which could change industries requiring complex calculations and sustainable technology, focusing on reducing environmental impacts. These trends will continue to shape how we live, work, and interact in the future, making our world smarter, more connected, and more efficient. Difficult words: revolutionize (to make a big change), autonomous (self-operating), immersive (deeply involving), complex (difficult to understand or find an answer to). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Technology is changing very fast and bringing many new ideas and inventions . Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are helping in areas like healthcare, finance, and education by making decisions without people. 5G is bringing faster internet and connecting many more devices, which will help smart cities and self-driving cars. The Internet of Things (IoT) connects devices like phones, cars, and refrigerators to make life easier. Blockchain, used in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, is helping with security in areas like finance. Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) are changing entertainment, gaming, and learning by giving people new experiences. Quantum Computing is a new technology that could help solve difficult problems. Sustainable technology is focused on helping the environment, using clean energy, and recycling. These technologies will make our future smarter and more connected. Difficult words: invention (a new creation), education (teaching and learning), cryptocurrency (digital money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Technology is changing our world. New ideas like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are helping in hospitals, finance, and education . 5G will make the internet faster. It will connect many more devices, like smart homes and self-driving cars. The Internet of Things (IoT) helps connect devices like phones and refrigerators to make our lives easier. Blockchain is a new way to keep things safe, especially in digital money. Augmented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) change gaming and give people new experiences. Sustainable technology is helping the world by using clean energy and recycling. These new technologies are changing how we live and work. Difficult words: education (teaching and learning), augmented (when you make something greater, larger, or more complete), sustainable (good for the natural world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Over 10,000 men in Aceh, a territory located at the northern end of Sumatra, broke the national record for the largest Saman dance performed simultaneously . Saman is one of the most popular dances in Indonesia and UNESCO recognised it in 2011. The dance of a thousand hands is traditionally performed by the Acehnese once a year to show unity after the harvest . The Director General of Culture explained that the event is a proof that common people still uphold their culture and the dance also shows tremendous unity of the people. Difficult words: simultaneously (at the same time), harvest (gathering crops – getting food from the field), tremendous (great). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Saman is a popular dance in Indonesia and UNESCO recognised it in 2011. It is also called the dance of a thousand hands. Over 10,000 men in Aceh, a territory in Sumatra, performed the dance. They broke the national record for the largest Saman dance. The Acehnese traditionally perform it once a year to show unity after the harvest . The Director General of Culture said that the event shows that people still uphold their culture. Difficult words: unity (togetherness – being close to one another), harvest (gathering crops – getting food from the fields), uphold (maintain, keep). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Saman is a popular dance in Indonesia. It is also called the dance of a thousand hands. More than 10,000 men do the dance. They set a new record. The men are from Aceh. Aceh is in Sumatra. They do the dance after the harvest . This shows their unity . Difficult words: harvest (getting food from the fields), unity (togetherness – being close to one another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

At Biopark Zoo in Barcelona, Spain, a mother zebra gave birth and her baby zebra fell into a pond within the exhibit . Two zookeepers moved into the pond to rescue the baby, and they put it on the side near its mother. Baby zebras can stand within 15 minutes of being born, and they can learn to walk within an hour to be able to survive in the wild. Difficult words: exhibit (a place where animals live inside of a zoo). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

At a zoo in Barcelona, Spain, a mother zebra gave birth and its baby zebra fell into a pond in their exhibit . Two zookeepers moved into the pond to rescue the baby. After birth, baby zebras can stand within 15 minutes. They can learn to walk within an hour to be able to survive in the wild. Difficult words: exhibit (a place where animals live in a zoo), zookeeper (a person who takes care of animals in a zoo), survive (live in a dangerous place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens at a zoo in Barcelona, Spain. A mother zebra gives birth. The baby zebra falls into a pond in the exhibit . Two zookeepers go into the pond to save the baby. Baby zebras learn very fast. After they are born, they can stand within 15 minutes. They learn to walk in an hour. Difficult words: pond (a small amount of water), exhibit (a place where animals live in a zoo), zookeeper (a person who cares for animals in a zoo). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The best TV shows of 2024 highlight diverse themes and storytelling. Shōgun, an FX series, combines action, history, and politics in 17th-century Japan, following an English sailor navigating a feudal society. Its rich visuals and compelling characters made it a massive hit. Industry on HBO expanded beyond its finance-driven drama to explore the moral challenges of green capitalism and personal ambition, offering sharp insights into corporate culture. FX’s Say Nothing delved into the Irish Troubles, focusing on Dolours Price, an IRA member haunted by her past. It raised complex questions about political violence. Other top shows include Pachinko (Apple TV+), exploring a Korean family’s struggles during WWII, and The Sympathizer (HBO), a visually bold take on the Vietnam War. Fantasmas (HBO) provided surreal humor, while Penelope (Netflix) told a meditative story of a teenager seeking purpose in the wilderness. Difficult words: feudal (related to medieval society and landownership), compelling (very exciting and interesting), bold (having a strong or clear appearance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The top TV shows of 2024 bring different stories to life. Shōgun (FX) tells about an English sailor in Japan in the 17th century. It is exciting with action, politics, and great characters. HBO’s Industry talks about people working in finance . This season shows how money and the environment create big problems for companies. FX’s Say Nothing is about Ireland’s Troubles. It focuses on Dolours Price, who feels bad about her past. Other shows include Pachinko (Apple TV+). It tells us about a Korean family in WWII, and The Sympathizer (HBO), a story about the Vietnam War. Fantasmas (HBO) is a funny show with strange stories, and Penelope (Netflix) is about a teenager who lives in the forest to find herself. Difficult words: finance (managing money), season (a series), environment (the natural world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The best TV shows of 2024 have many stories. Shōgun (FX) is about a sailor in Japan long ago. It has fights, history, and great characters . Industry (HBO) is about young people who work with money. They have problems with work and life. Say Nothing (FX) is about Ireland and a woman who remembers her past. Other shows include Pachinko (Apple TV+), about a family during a war, and The Sympathizer (HBO), about Vietnam. Fantasmas (HBO) is a funny and strange show. Penelope (Netflix) is about a girl who lives in the woods to think about her life. Difficult words: sailor (a person who works on a ship), character (a person in a play, film, or novel), woods (a place with many trees). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The story of a raccoon turned viral when it decided to climb up a 25-storey building in Minnesota, USA. It started its journey up on Monday. Maintenance workers tried to get the animal down, but it simply ignored them. To everyone’s amazement, the heroic racoon made it to the 23rd storey before taking a break on the windowsill. The director of the ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ (in which one character is an anthropomorphic raccoon) even offered $1,000 to get it down. The climber’s way up progressed and everyone celebrated after it got all the way to the top in the early hours of Wednesday. Difficult words: viral (very popular, especially on the Internet), anthropomorphic (human-like), progress (go on, continue). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A raccoon in Minnesota, USA, decided to climb up a 25-storey building one day. It started its journey on Monday, and workers tried to get it down, but it ignored them. The story of the heroic raccoon soon became viral . The director of the ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ (in which one character is an anthropomorphic raccoon) even offered $1,000 to get it down. The animal kept going until the 23rd storey where arested on a windowsill . It made it to the top in the early hours of Wednesday. Difficult words: viral (very popular, especially on the Internet), anthropomorphic (human-like), windowsill (a flat area outside a window). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This story is about a raccoon. It starts climbing up a building in Minnesota, USA. It starts on Monday. People try to get it down. The animal does not want to come down. It continues up. The raccoon becomes popular. People want to know how its story ends. It climbs up to the 23rd storey . It relaxes there for a while. On Wednesday morning, it makes it to the top. Difficult words: climb (go up), continue (keep going), storey (a floor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Norwegian veteran Tarjei Boe made an impressive comeback after a difficult start to the season, winning the 15 km Mass Start at Annecy Le Grand Bornand at 37:20.8. Despite challenging track conditions due to heavy rain, Boe performed steadily, focusing on accuracy during the shooting stages. The Norwegian team dominated the race, with Johannes Thingnes Boe and other strong contenders also competing. A crucial part of the race was maintaining a balance between speed and precision in shooting, as missing targets made it harder to stay in the lead. Young athletes showed confidence, pushing the pace early, while veterans like Sturla Holm Lægreid demonstrated consistency. Boe’s victory was especially significant as it qualified him for future championships, proving his resilience despite earlier setbacks. His brother Johannes expressed joy over Tarjei’s success, highlighting their close bond. Overall, it was a thrilling race that showed both individual skill and team dominance . Difficult words: contender (a person competing for a prize or position), resilience (the ability to recover from difficulties), dominance (having strong control or influence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Tarjei Boe won the 15 km Mass Start race in Annecy Le Grand Bornand at 37:20.8. The race was difficult because of heavy rain, which made the track soft. Boe stayed focused and shot well, which helped him stay ahead. The Norwegian team did very well, with many athletes in top places. The race was exciting because young athletes tried to set a fast pace while others stayed calm and waited for the right time to push. Missing targets made it harder for many racers to catch up. Boe’s win was important because it helped him qualify for future championships. His brother Johannes was very happy for him, which showed their strong family support. Difficult words: focused (looking at or listening to someone or something with full attention), pace (the speed of walking or running), qualify (to succeed in getting into a competition). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Tarjei Boe from Norway wins a big race in Annecy Le Grand Bornand. He finishes in 37:20.8. The track is hard to ski because of heavy rain. The rain makes the track soft. Boe is very good at shooting. It helps him win. The Norwegian team does well. Many racers are in the top positions. The race is exciting . Young racers started fast. But Boe stays calm. He waits to go faster later. Many racers miss their targets. It is hard for them to win. Boe’s win is important for his future races. His brother Johannes is very happy for him and proud of his success. Difficult words: race (a competition of speed), exciting (making you feel excited and happy), proud (feeling happy because you or someone else does something great). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of people visited Stonehenge and other historic sites to celebrate the winter solstice, the shortest day of the year. Despite cloudy skies and strong winds, the crowd gathered early to witness the sunrise at 8:09 GMT, marking the start of longer days. Stonehenge opens to the public during the summer and winter solstices, offering a unique opportunity to experience its alignment with the sun. A visitor shared that he came to reflect on the past year and look forward to renewal in the new year. Attendees described the event as a spiritual and joyful experience, drawing people from diverse backgrounds. In nearby Avebury, participants followed pagan traditions like tying ribbons to trees as prayers or memories. Glastonbury Tor also welcomed visitors for singing and ceremonies at sunrise. These events, deeply connected to ancient traditions, remind people of the natural cycles and their significance in human life. Difficult words: alignment (arrangement in a straight line or proper position), renewal (starting again in a positive way), pagan (belonging to a religion that worships gods that existed before main world religions). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people came to Stonehenge to celebrate the winter solstice, the shortest day of the year. The sunrise at 8:09 GMT marked the start of longer days. Visitors gathered early, although it was windy weather. They enjoyed the event’s spiritual and happy atmosphere. Stonehenge, which is usually closed, opens for this special day because the stones align with the sun during solstices. A visitor said he wanted to think about the past year and prepare for the new one. In Avebury, people tied ribbons to trees, a tradition to honor loved ones or pray. Glastonbury Tor also had celebrations with singing and rituals . These events connect people to old traditions and nature. Difficult words: gather (to meet), align (to match up in a straight line or position), ritual (actions which people do for a specific purpose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Stonehenge is special during the winter solstice , the shortest day of the year. Many people come early in the morning to see the sunrise. This day is important because it starts longer days. The stones at Stonehenge match the sun’s position. Stonehenge opens to the public for this event. People say that they feel happy and connected. One visitor comes to think about the past year and start fresh. In Avebury, people tie ribbons on trees. They remember people they love. At Glastonbury Tor, there is singing and fire. These places are part of old traditions and nature. Difficult words: solstice (the shortest or longest day of the year), ribbon (a long thin piece of fabric), tradition (what people usually do, and they do it for a long time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Florida, a 28-year old man stole a tractor and was driving it down the road when he noticed that police were pursuing him because of his erratic driving. At first, he complied with a search by the police, but then he became violent and tried to escape by running away. The policeman used a taser to stop him, arrested him, and took him to hospital. Difficult words: pursue (follow closely to try to catch someone), erratic (unusual), comply (follow orders). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Florida, a man stole a tractor and was driving it down the road. Police started to follow him because he was driving erratically . The police asked the man to pull over. At first, he complied when the police wanted to search him, but then he became violent and began to run away. The policeman used a taser to stop him. Then he arrested him and took him to hospital. Difficult words: erratically (unusually doing something), comply (be OK with something), search (when police check if a person has something illegal on him or her). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Florida, a man steals a tractor. He drives it down the road. He drives erratically . Police see his driving. They drive behind him. Then, the police ask the man to stop. At first, he does as they tell him. Then he becomes violent . He starts running away. One policeman uses a taser . It hits the man. It makes him fall down. The policeman arrests him. Then he takes him to hospital. Difficult words: erratically (not normal), violent (a violent person wants to hurt or kill you), taser (an electric weapon that police use to stop people without killing them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Russia, a woman was taking a selfie at an art show and leaned against a wall display , which then fell over onto two paintings by artists Salvador Dali and Francisco Goya . The paintings were valuable and the fall badly damaged them. Difficult words: wall display (a light wall that people can hang art on to make exhibits within a museum or an art show), Salvador Dali (an important Spanish painter from the 1900s who painted in the surrealist style – a style focused on showing what is inside the mind and in dreams), Francisco Goya (an important Spanish painter from the 1700s to the 1800s who painted in the Romantic style – a style focused on nature, beauty and imagination), valuable (culturally important and worth a lot of money). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Russia, a woman leaned on a wall display at an art show to take a selfie. She accidentally knocked the display over on top of two paintings by two important Spanish artists – Salvador Dali and Francisco Goya. The paintings were valuable and the falling wall damaged them. Difficult words: wall display (a wall that people can move and can hang art for a museum or an art show), valuable (culturally important and worth a lot of money), damage (hurt or break something badly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A woman is at an art show in Russia. She wants to take a selfie. She leans against a wall display . When she leans, the wall falls over. It falls on top of paintings. The paintings are by two important Spanish artists. The paintings cost a lot of money. The fall breaks them. Difficult words: lean (stand at an angle, do not stand straight), wall display (a light wall on which people put pictures for an art show). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A 50-year-old Saudi doctor drove his car into a busy Christmas market in Magdeburg, Germany, killing at least four people, including a child, and injuring over 68 others, with 15 in serious condition. The market, a popular event attracting many visitors, turned into chaos as the car sped through a gap in the concrete barriers designed for safety. The suspect, who had lived in Germany for 18 years and worked as a doctor, acted alone. Authorities quickly arrested him and confirmed no explosives were found in his car. The suspect had no criminal record and had previously criticized Islam publicly. Police have launched an investigation into the motive , which remains unclear. German Chancellor Olaf Scholz expressed condolences and visited the scene. The incident has raised concerns about security at public events and possible political exploitation by far-right groups ahead of upcoming elections. Nearby markets have increased security measures. Difficult words: motive (a reason for doing something), exploitation (using something for personal gain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man drove his car into a Christmas market in Magdeburg, Germany. He killed four people, including a child, and hurt over 68 others. The incident happened on Friday night when the market was full of visitors. The car entered through a gap in safety blocks . People tried to help the injured while police and doctors arrived quickly. The driver was a 50-year-old Saudi doctor who lived in Germany for 18 years, and police arrested him at the scene. Police confirmed that he acted alone, and they found no bombs in his car. The man had no criminal record , and police don’t know his reasons for doing that. Germany’s leader, Olaf Scholz, shared his sadness and visited the area. Other markets in Germany increased security . Difficult words: safety block (a block which you cannot move, and it makes a place safe), criminal record (a list of a person’s previous crimes), security (being safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Germany, a car hits people at a Christmas market in Magdeburg. Four people die, including a child, and over 68 are hurt. Police stop the driver. The driver is a 50-year-old doctor from Saudi Arabia. He lives in Germany for 18 years. The man does nothing wrong in the past. Police do not know why he does this. The market is busy when the car drives fast through a gap in the safety blocks . Many people are scared. They try to help others. The police and doctors come quickly. Germany’s leader says that he feels sorry for the victims . Other markets in Germany are now more secure . Gukesh Dommaraju, an 18-year-old from India, has become the youngest world chess champion in history. He defeated Ding Liren from China during a 14-game tournament in Singapore. Gukesh’s win was historic, as he broke the record set by Garry Kasparov, who became champion at age 22. This victory made Gukesh a national hero in India, a country where cricket is usually the most celebrated sport. When he arrived at the airport in Chennai, fans welcomed him with cheers, flowers, and posters. Gukesh thanked them, saying it felt amazing to bring the trophy back to India. Students from his school held placards celebrating his success. Gukesh, who became a grandmaster at the age of 12, has inspired many young people to pursue chess professionally. His father has supported him throughout his career. Gukesh is only the second Indian to win the title, following Viswanathan Anand. He will be honored by the government and meet Prime Minister Modi later this month. Difficult words: placard (a sign or poster with messages or pictures), pursue (to follow). William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, an influential scholar and activist, is celebrated in an animated documentary short exploring his life and work. Du Bois’ book, The Souls of Black Folk, examines the dual identity of African Americans. A pioneer in anti-racist thought, Du Bois used data and infographics to challenge myths of Black inferiority . His science fiction story The Comet (1920) imagined a world where segregation briefly vanished in the aftermath of an apocalyptic event. His life in Atlanta during the 1906 race riots also inspired his writings on racial violence. Du Bois was a founder of the NAACP, advocating for civil rights and exposing the color line that segregated African Americans. He introduced double consciousness, the sense of seeing oneself through others’ eyes, as a way to understand the divided African-American experience. Difficult words: pioneer (a person who does something first), inferiority (being lower in status or quality than others), segregation (separation of groups), aftermath (the consequences or after-effects of an unpleasant event). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Du Bois used facts and pictures to show that Black people are equal to others. In 1920, he wrote a story called The Comet about a disaster that ended segregation for a short time. He also lived during the 1906 Atlanta riots , where many Black people were hurt. Du Bois helped start the NAACP, the first group to fight for civil rights in America. He wrote about double consciousness, the feeling of being between two worlds. He loved sad songs, which gave strength and hope to African Americans. Difficult words: equal (the same), segregation (keeping groups apart), riot (a protest). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Difficult words: treatment (how someone behaves towards you), fact (a true thing), disaster (an event which hurts many people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Turkey will receive an additional one billion euros from the EU to assist Syrian refugees living in the country. This decision was announced by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen after discussions with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. Both leaders emphasized the importance of stability and unity in Syria. The funds aim to support Turkey, which hosts approximately four million Syrian refugees, with education, healthcare, and social services. Von der Leyen highlighted the EU’s commitment to helping Turkey facilitate the voluntary return of refugees to Syria. Additionally, the EU plans to enhance its engagement with Syria’s Islamist-led government to prevent the resurgence of extremist groups like ISIS. Turkey, seen as a key player in the region, has strong ties with Syrian rebel leaders. Erdogan views this funding as a diplomatic success, but Turkey continues to press for the lifting of economic sanctions on Syria to enable reconstruction. Difficult words: facilitate (to make a process easier), enhance (increase, or intensify), resurgence (a rising again into life or activity). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A widely used social media app, TikTok, faces a potential ban in the US, set to take effect on January 19th. However, TikTok has asked the Supreme Court to block the ban, arguing it violates free speech. Interestingly, President-elect Trump, who previously criticized TikTok as a threat to national security, now appears to be reconsidering. This change is attributed to his positive perception of TikTok’s role in the 2024 election results. Trump recently met TikTok’s CEO to discuss the app’s future. TikTok’s parent company, ByteDance, has also been ordered to sell the app to avoid the ban. A one-month ban could cost 1 billion dollars in economic losses, impacting users, businesses, and content creators. While TikTok seeks a quick resolution through the courts, it remains uncertain whether Trump’s administration will actively repeal the legislation or delay enforcement. Time is critical as January 20th approaches. Difficult words: attribute (to regard something as being caused by), perception (how something is regarded or understood), repeal (to remove the legal force of law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
